a7aeecfe-a923-4537-8218-49f1f98c038d.summary_md: Jesse closed Season 26 at 12-1 with a commanding +1396 aggregate spread, the only blemish a 360-366 nail-biter to Kumba Obey in Round 10, while blowouts like +178 over LoveLetters and +176 over Allen Pengelly padded the margin. Bingo-finding was sharp at 33/35 (94.3%), nearly double the opposition's 50% rate, with opponents missing a parade of bingos — three apiece from Allen Pengelly and K2O, plus two from Matthew Salmon. Most of the win-probability bleed came early in games (28 errors, 64.4% win prob lost, half the total damage), with ordinary tactical misses outweighing the two missed bingos (DA(H)ABiYA, BIOMe(T)RY); the single costliest error was the Round 10 pre-endgame turn against Kumba Obey, cashing in 2J CIN(Q)S for 44 instead of the far stronger 2M (Q)I, which cost 17.4% win probability in that tight loss. Since the challenge rule was void, no phonies were possible for either side, so the clean word choices here reflect the format rather than discipline.
a7aeecfe-a923-4537-8218-49f1f98c038d.title: Collins League - Season 26

b2aa32e7-ab1d-45c2-8d59-362eeec37cb1.summary_md: Jesse finished 20-9 (+1689) at NSC 2019, bookended by a brutal five-loss stretch across Rounds 9–14 and a strong 13-2 closing run that included a 580-point demolition of Jason Keller in Round 26. Bingo-finding was excellent at 97.4% (76/78), but five phonies — including RINGL(E)TY and (COFFEE)POTS — were played, costing dearly since they were never challenged off. Win probability actually bled away most in the mid-game (144.7% lost over 56 errors) and early game (142.5% over 58 errors), with pre-endgame contributing a smaller 76.6%, while the endgame cost 0% win probability despite 113 equity lost; ordinary tactical errors dominated over the two missed bingos (32.6% combined). The single costliest mistake came in Round 27 against Josh Castellano, passing a GILNRTY rack instead of bingoing RINGL(E)TY for 63 — a 23.5% win-probability swing in a game ultimately lost 451-473.

c0709ecf-1a40-4a10-8706-732ab3d5ba75.summary_md: Jesse went 14-6 (+800 spread) at the Crescent City Cup, with marquee wins over Stefan Rau (567-334) and Peter Armstrong (543-303), and three losses to Evan Berofsky across their matchups including a brutal 317-405 finale. Win probability bled away mostly in the pre-endgame (140.6% lost over 26 errors) and mid-game (122.8% over 39 errors), more than either the early or endgame stretches, and the damage came overwhelmingly from ordinary tactical misplays rather than missed bingos — the two whiffed bingos ((I)NDUCIAE and SEA(S)ONAL) cost 29.8% between them, a fraction of the total 364%. The single costliest blunder was Round 1 against Sandy Nang, passing up L6 NIL for N10 PEN, which alone cost 38.2% win probability. Bingo-finding was otherwise sharp at 52/54 (96.3%), and the collection carried just one phony (RAVI/DADA* vs. Ben Schoenbrun) against four from opponents, including Robert Linn's unchallenged PIROGHIS/OP* and PIROGS/DOUANIERS* in the Round 6 loss.
c0709ecf-1a40-4a10-8706-732ab3d5ba75.title: Crescent City Cup 2019

c29206c8-3491-4297-87d4-a3fab33e7d10.summary_md: Jesse closed out Collins League Season 24 at 11-3 (+1052), highlighted by a dominant +208 blowout over dang3rous in Round 5 and strong wins over hiiamrayne (+157) and Dieter Jedamski (+158), with the only real setbacks coming against wajin (−121), oisín 𓃩 (−47), and a tight −10 loss to Chee Meng Lee. Across the 84 logged errors, win probability bled away most in the mid-game (31 errors, 41% of the loss) and pre-endgame (38%), while the endgame stage cost nothing in win probability despite 110 equity lost on spread-only misplays; ordinary tactical misses dominated over bingo-finding lapses, with the single costliest blunder coming in Round 13 against Chee Meng Lee, where Jesse played B6 BA for 28 instead of the far stronger 11I FEN, a 43.8% win-probability swing. Bingo-finding was otherwise sharp at 92.6% (25/27), well clear of opponents' 48.8%, and strong game management carried through despite the void challenge rule structurally limiting what errors could even occur.

cf677d39-81ad-4a59-aec9-227c38340572.summary_md: Jesse finished 9-10 (+144) at Causeway 2026, a middling record built on wild swings — a 605-point demolition of Austin Shin and a +161 rout of Vannitha Balasingam offset by three double-digit losses, including a −193 blowout to Josh Castellano. Errors were spread fairly evenly across the game but win probability actually bled out most in the mid-game (38 errors, 124.5% of win% lost, 37% of the total), with missed bingos a real factor (10 instances, 113.7% win% lost) though ordinary tactical misplays were just as numerous; the single costliest error was Rd19 against Odette Rio, cashing in 7L (E)MO for 15 instead of 9D CLIME for 22, a 28.2% win-probability swing in a game ultimately lost by just two points.

d1212bee-bc38-4f19-8619-6be460686182.summary_md: Jesse went 5-1 with a +500 aggregate spread in this Austin one-day, beating Michael Donegan, Anuj Shetty, James Curley, and Becky Dyer twice, with the lone loss coming to Chris Canik at 384-437. Play was mostly sharp — a 12/14 (85.7%) bingo find rate and only one phony (Anuj Shetty's GU/PU) — though the Round 3 game against Curley was costly, missing both COURAN(T)O and DOGGEDl(Y), which together account for the two biggest win-probability swings of the collection. Across 35 tracked errors the win probability actually bled out mostly in the pre-endgame stage (29.8% of the loss despite just 4 errors) and early stage (25.1% over 8 errors), while the endgame errors, though numerous (8) and equity-costly (91 points), cost 0% win probability; missed bingos were a small but disproportionate share of the damage (2 errors, 28.2% of win probability lost). The single worst moment was in Round 5 against Canik: with ?CCILNO on turn 23, Jesse played O6 ICON for 27 instead of the far superior 13C (R)OC for 5, bleeding 26.9% win probability.
d1212bee-bc38-4f19-8619-6be460686182.title: Austin One-Day Aug '23

e87cdf09-ffc4-477b-ae68-95cc8856e101.summary_md: Jesse finished 18-18 (+206) at Causeway 2016, a grueling round robin against a murderers' row that included five meetings with Nigel Richards (2-3), plus Mark Nyman, Dave Wiegand, and David Eldar multiple times each. Most of the win probability actually bled away in the mid-game (78 errors, 349.1% win% lost, 42% of the total) rather than early or late, and while eight missed bingos cost real equity, ordinary tactical misplays did the heavier damage — the single costliest was Round 18 against Chollapat, passing with AAEIORS instead of playing the phony 3H AI, which alone cost 66.4% win probability. Jesse's bingo-finding was strong overall at 91.6% (87/95), essentially matching opponents' 92.9%, and phony plays like PARTEDLY*, FLIES*/TIZE*/VIGAS*, and ARIOSA*/SI*/AN* were a recurring drag on results. A brutal middle stretch — five straight losses through Rounds 29-34 against Eldar, Nyman, Richards, and Wiegand — undid the promise of a strong 8-4 start built on wins like the +185 rout of Nyman in Round 27.
e87cdf09-ffc4-477b-ae68-95cc8856e101.title: Causeway 2016

ffe31e07-d5fb-4937-bc08-691958053a8e.summary_md: Jesse Day fell 1-3 to Nigel Richards in the 2018 World Championship final, a −214 aggregate swing punctuated by a lone Round 1 blowout win (541-391) before three straight losses, including a heartbreaking 12-point Round 3 defeat. The bulk of the damage came early in games — 11 errors there cost 39.7% win probability, dwarfing mid-game (17.4%), pre-endgame (7.5%), and endgame (0%) losses — and missed bingos were a real factor, accounting for 30.6% of win probability lost across just three whiffs. The single costliest moment was in Round 1, turn 7, where Jesse played E7 D(EF)OG for 20 instead of finding 3C DOGSTAI(L) for 74, bleeding 19.0% win probability and 45.8 points of equity. Nigel, for his part, played a near-perfect match, missing only one bingo (WISELIER) all event while converting his chances with brutal efficiency.
